narrative: In a compound magnitude 7.2 earthquake and 7-foot king tide scenario, failure cascades outward from the perimeter seawall and electric substations. Breaching the seawall exposes substations, fuel handling, the ferry terminal, and evacuation routes, while substation outages cripple communications and high-pressure water pumps. The $958M 1-in-100 tail loss (VaR99) is driven by compound failures where simultaneous seawall, substation, and bridge approach disruptions sever downstream evacuation roads and firefighting water pumps, which suffer the highest baseline failure probabilities at 23.3% and 21.3%. The proposed portfolio breaks this chain by stabilizing the seawall via jet grouting and floodgates, hardening substations with elevation, base isolation, and microgrid islanding, and adding redundant backup power, flexible joints, and soil stabilization to critical downstream lifelines. Note that this model is a stylized demo, not an engineering estimate.
